verification_report.summary: The full assembled chain is correct under the explicitly accepted classical and internal inputs. The ample-locus theorem applies to every big closed class, without nefness: BEGZ supplies the unique normalized full-mass minimal-singularity solution for the smooth global density; the strict analytic current identifies the regular locus with Amp(alpha); non-pluripolar and local bounded Bedford-Taylor measures agree there; the reconstructed Dang theorem supplies local Holder continuity from the global Lp density; and the nonclosed interior theorem upgrades Holder continuity to smooth strict positivity. The reconstructed Holder proof correctly handles the reference-preserving subsolution, normalized comparison potential, Demailly Chern-flow expansion with a genuine O(delta) smooth-background error, the unbounded L1 O(delta^2) smoothing bound, positive minimizing radius, and local interpolation. The interior bootstrap correctly establishes proper localization, exact smooth Dirichlet approximants with polynomial boundary trace, subpower trace localization, gradient interpolation, polynomial Chern-Calabi control, nonlinear trace recovery, and the ABP strong-to-viscosity/Evans-Krylov/Schauder step. Local/global measure transitions, the analytic pole set, dimension one, and the dd^c=i/(2pi) convention are handled consistently. No bounded-mass or positive-lower-mass property is used. Smoothness of the density only on Omega is not used to invoke Dang: the local theorem retains Holder continuity as a premise, while the global volume-form application discharges it through global Lp integrability. No whole-book certification or novelty conclusion is implied.
